summary: Pre-Vote update modeled (MODEL_CHANGE_REQUIRED); traces validated; two update-introduced model-checking findings; confirmation (Part 4) not executed in this run.
validation_limits: Bounded three-node model; no full-model BFS exhausted its queue within the 30-minute budgets.
The livelock witness was found under a pruning-only search monitor; liveness is checked as a safety witness plus exhaustive closure from the witness, without fairness assumptions.
Multi-node schedules were not replayed on the real runtime; the per-node mechanisms were observed on the real Engine (spec/output/observations.log).

findings.title: Pre-Vote can leave a live majority permanently leaderless
findings.cause: Pre-Vote never transfers vote information: handle_pre_vote_resp ignores a rejecting responder's higher vote and handle_pre_vote_req rejects Pre-Votes below the local vote, so a lower-term voter with the longest log and higher-term voters with shorter logs reject each other forever.
findings.trigger: Three voters with Pre-Vote on: node 3 wins a Pre-Vote quorum and starts a term-2 election that node 2 refuses after receiving the leader's last entry; the leader then crashes.
findings.consequence: The two live voters never elect a leader until the crashed node returns or an operator forces a real election.

findings.title: A stale Pre-Vote round demotes a newly established leader
findings.cause: establish_leader/become_leader keep Engine.pre_candidate and handle_pre_vote_resp does not check the node's role, so a Pre-Vote round started while the node was still a Candidate later calls elect() on the Leader.
findings.trigger: A Candidate's election tick runs pre_elect while its real election is open; the real election succeeds; a granted Pre-Vote response then arrives.
findings.consequence: The new leader steps down to Candidate and bumps the term without any failure.
